title: Melatonin impedes NCOA4/ACSL4-dependent ferroptosis by targeting STING to ameliorate diabetic cognitive dysfunction.
authors: Xu, Tao; Xie, Zhaoyu; Zhao, Yongting; Ren, Zhengrui; Wu, Miaomiao; Zhu, Zhixu; Meng, Han; Zhang, Yu; Wan, Mengqi; Chen, Chao; Han, Jun; Che, Hui
one_liner_zh: 该文研究褪黑素通过靶向STING抑制铁死亡和铁蛋白自噬改善糖尿病认知障碍，属于纯医学/细胞机制研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Melatonin (MLT) is a potentially effective therapeutic agent for mitigating brain injury under various pathological conditions. However, the molecular mechanisms of its ability to ameliorate diabetic cognitive dysfunction (DCD) require further elucidation. In this study, we demonstrated that MLT administration improved the learning and memory deficits in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mice, concurrently attenuated acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) - dependent ferroptosis in diabetic brain tissue and neuronal cells exposed to high glucose/palmitic acid (HG + PA), as indicated by reduced lipid peroxidation, elevated GSH and SOD levels, increased GPX4 levels, and downregulated ACSL4 expression. Furthermore, MLT reversed nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4) -mediated ferritinophagy in vivo and in vitro. This opinion was demonstrated by decreased intracellular ROS and Fe(2+) levels, reduced NCOA4 expression, and increased Ferritin levels. Mechanistic investigations revealed that MLT directly binds to stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and suppresses its expression and activation, as determined by surface plasmon resonance, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assays. Consequently, MLT treatment disrupted the subsequent recruitment of NCOA4 and ACSL4 to STING. Pharmacological activation or genetic overexpression of STING attenuated the inhibitory effect of MLT on ferroptosis and ferritinophagy. In contrast, STING silencing had the opposite effects under the aforementioned conditions. Our findings revealed that melatonin exerts dual regulatory mechanisms, inhibiting ACSL4-dependent ferroptosis and suppressing NCOA4 axis-mediated ferritinophagy through directly targeting STING, thereby ameliorating diabetic cognitive dysfunction.
abstract_zh: 褪黑素（MLT）是一种在多种病理条件下减轻脑损伤的潜在有效治疗剂。然而，其改善糖尿病认知功能障碍（DCD）的分子机制仍需进一步阐明。在本研究中，我们证明MLT给药改善了2型糖尿病（T2DM）小鼠的学习和记忆缺陷，同时减轻了糖尿病脑组织及暴露于高糖/棕榈酸（HG + PA）的神经元细胞中酰基辅酶A合成酶长链家族成员4（ACSL4）依赖性铁死亡，表现为脂质过氧化减少、GSH和SOD水平升高、GPX4水平增加以及ACSL4表达下调。此外，MLT在体内和体外逆转了核受体共激活因子4（NCOA4）介导的铁蛋白自噬。这一观点通过细胞内ROS和Fe(2+)水平降低、NCOA4表达减少以及铁蛋白水平升高得到证实。机制研究表明，MLT直接结合干扰素基因刺激因子（STING）并抑制其表达和激活，这通过表面等离子体共振、分子对接和细胞热位移实验确定。因此，MLT处理破坏了随后NCOA4和ACSL4向STING的募集。STING的药理学激活或基因过表达减弱了MLT对铁死亡和铁蛋白自噬的抑制作用。相反，在上述条件下，STING沉默则产生相反效果。我们的发现揭示，褪黑素通过直接靶向STING发挥双重调节机制，抑制ACSL4依赖性铁死亡并抑制NCOA4轴介导的铁蛋白自噬，从而改善糖尿病认知功能障碍。
